narrative:
Your application was denied because an automated assessment estimated an 82.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That high failure risk, not a judgment about your potential as a lawyer, is what triggered the rejection; gender and race were not used in the decision.

The strongest factor was your third-year decile placement. You are recorded in decile 1, while accepted students averaged about decile 5.79, and this factor pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your first-year decile placement. Again recorded as decile 1 against an accepted-student average of about 6, it also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your LSAT score of 35, below the accepted-student average of 37.18. This factor pushed toward passing, but it was not strong enough to offset the two academic-standing measures.

To move forward, ask admissions for a human review and clarify whether updated grades, a retaken LSAT, or an explanatory statement about any special circumstances can be considered. Speak with a prelaw advisor about strengthening your LSAT preparation and academic record. You may also ask whether a delayed application, conditional admission, or another law program would be more appropriate given this assessment.
